title: arXiv Mathematics — weekly notable papers, 10–16 October 2026
global_caveat: Inferred, significance-led selection; arXiv has no official trending chart, and independent attention/citation data are too limited for a popularity ranking. Results are author-attributed preprint claims, not independently checked proofs.

sections.title: The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields
sections.abstract: The authors prove that each degree-n number field of absolute discriminant D has a defining integral polynomial with coefficient sizes O_n(√D), resolving a conjecture of Ruppert.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1 gives a degree-n generator with an integral degree-n polynomial whose height is bounded by a constant depending on n times √D_K.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Arbitrary number fields; the implied constant depends on degree n. The authors say the proof does not assume the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound is O_n and is not uniform in n.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The claimed bound applies to every number field of fixed degree and settles the stated 1998 conjecture; the proof combines ideal-lattice geometry with an averaged zeta-function argument.

sections.title: A proof of the rational exponents conjecture
sections.abstract: For every rational r in [1,2], the authors claim a graph H with extremal number ex(n,H)=Θ(n^r), the Erdős–Simonovits rational exponents conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the conjecture by combining Bukh–Conlon lower bounds with an upper-bound theorem for subdivisions of connected bipartite graphs.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Existentially, for finite graphs H and rational exponents r in [1,2], with asymptotics in the number of vertices n.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe this as a proof of the result claimed by Epoch AI and situate it in prior combinatorial work; this remains an attributed preprint result.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The stated result covers the full rational exponent interval, rather than one subrange; a subdivision upper-bound theorem is the technical step used to propagate to all exponents.

sections.title: Superdiffusive Invariance Principle for the two-dimensional Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
sections.abstract: For two-dimensional ASEP, the paper derives logarithmically enhanced longitudinal diffusivity and proves convergence of the rescaled density-fluctuation field to a conservative stochastic heat equation.
sections.claimed_result: The fluctuation field converges under anisotropic scaling to the specified Gaussian fixed point; a superdiffusive central limit theorem follows for the second-class particle.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bernoulli product initial law with density in (0,1); finite-range jump kernel, nonzero drift, and uniaxial asymmetry in dimension two.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated hypotheses restrict the result to the two-dimensional, finite-range, uniaxially asymmetric regime.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors state this is the first space-time scaling-limit result for a nonequilibrium interacting particle system at its critical dimension; it also derives a second-class-particle limit.

sections.title: Proof of the Penrose Conjecture for Maximally Parameterized Initial Data Sets
sections.abstract: The authors prove the spacetime Penrose inequality in every dimension n≥3 for asymptotically flat initial data in a specified maximally parameterized class, under the dominant energy condition.
sections.claimed_result: For the stated class, the authors construct a nonnegative-scalar-curvature comparison metric and derive the Penrose bound subject to horizon-completion and asymptotic hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Asymptotically flat data satisfying the dominant energy condition and having the paper's maximally parameterized form, plus a horizon nondegeneracy condition and regularity of the comparison metric.
sections.unique_caveat: Not a proof for arbitrary initial data; the authors leave a degenerate PDE existence problem and global surjectivity unresolved and exclude some degenerate horizon ends.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An all-dimensional result for a major geometric inequality, reducing the target case to the Riemannian Penrose inequality using a new Schoen–Yau identity.

sections.title: Effective equidistribution of polynomial trajectories in SL₃(R)/SL₃(Z)
sections.abstract: For fixed matrix-polynomial trajectories on the SL₃ lattice quotient, the author gives an intrinsic Diophantine criterion for power-rate equidistribution on the homogeneous orbit closure.
sections.claimed_result: The author classifies possible orbit-closure groups and combines quantitative nilmanifold equidistribution, unipotent approximation, and effective flow estimates to prove the criterion.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A fixed matrix-polynomial trajectory in SL₃(R)/SL₃(Z), with equidistribution on its homogeneous orbit closure under the stated Diophantine condition.
sections.unique_caveat: Specialized to the SL₃ quotient; the abstract does not claim a corresponding criterion for higher-rank SLₙ quotients.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The necessary-and-sufficient criterion uses polynomial tests of degree at most two, independent of trajectory degree, and links dynamics with number theory.

sections.title: Supercritical sharpness for Ising double random currents
sections.abstract: The authors establish local uniqueness of the macroscopic cluster in the double-random-current representation of the Ising model throughout the supercritical regime.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive local uniqueness with high probability and recover exponential decay of truncated Ising correlations and exponential mixing for the FK-Ising measure using a sprinkling argument.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Double random current on Z^d, d≥3, at β>β_c, uniformly over source boundary conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract says the correlation-decay and FK-mixing consequences were previously obtained; the stated advance is a simpler proof route.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result is uniform over boundary sources for every β>β_c in d≥3 and supplies standard renormalization consequences, including exponential mixing.

sections.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
sections.abstract: The revised paper proves that an avalanche triggered at the origin in the stationary abelian sandpile on Z² has finitely many topplings.
sections.claimed_result: Almost surely, adding a grain at the origin to the infinite-volume stationary sandpile in dimension two produces only finitely many topplings.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Abelian sandpile on Z² in the stationary state defined through finite boxes with absorbing boundary.
sections.unique_caveat: Establishes finiteness, not a tail estimate or quantitative bound on avalanche size.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Settles a question attributed to Athreya and Járai for the previously unresolved two-dimensional case; the revised version lists a Lean 4 formalization.

sections.title: All Serrin bands are unduloidal
sections.abstract: The authors show that every planar Serrin domain with two boundary components belongs to the canonical unduloidal family.
sections.claimed_result: Any Serrin domain in R² with two boundary components is a member of the canonical unduloidal family.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Planar Serrin domain with exactly two boundary components.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not extend the classification to higher dimensions or other boundary-component counts.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A full classification within a geometrically specific overdetermined elliptic setting, connecting PDE and differential geometry.
